ElevenLabs Pro: AI Voice Synthesis and Cloning Platform for Windows

A Windows reference and setup guide for the ElevenLabs Pro AI voice platform, text-to-speech generation, voice cloning capabilities, and the first-run workflow.

## Introduction Elevenlabs Pro is an AI voice synthesis platform for Windows that turns written text into natural-sounding speech, lets you build custom voice clones, and dubs content into multiple languages. It is used by beginners exploring AI audio for the first time as well as professionals producing narration, audiobooks, podcasts, and localized video content. Whether you are testing a single line of dialogue or managing a full multilingual project, the platform gives you a single workspace to work in. When you use Elevenlabs Pro you get a text-to-speech engine with fine control over tone and delivery, a voice library to manage your own cloned voices, and a dubbing workflow for translating spoken audio. The typical flow is simple: you write or paste your script, assign a voice, adjust the settings, preview the result, and export the audio you need. This makes it practical to move from an idea to a finished voice track in a few focused steps. In the wider field of AI audio, Elevenlabs Pro sits at the intersection of speech synthesis and creative production. The platform is extensible through voice design and API-style integrations, and its community shares prompt tips, voice presets, and dubbing workflows. The product continues to evolve with new voice models and language support, so it is worth keeping your installation current. #

candidates.readme_excerpt:
Izwi

Open-source voice AI that runs on your machine.

Website - Documentation - Releases - Issues

Izwi runs speech recognition, text-to-speech, voice chat, and chat models on your own machine. Use it as a desktop app, a web UI, or a CLI, or point your own apps and phone lines at its OpenAI-compatible server. Models download once from Hugging Face; after that, inference runs entirely on your machine, with no cloud service or API key. ## What It Does ### In the app - **Voice:** talk with a local assistant. The Standard engine chains speech recognition, chat, and TTS models; the Compact engine uses one speech-to-speech model (LFM3 Audio). Give it tools from MCP servers, let agents hand the conversation to each other, and turn on memory so it keeps your preferences. - **Dictation** (desktop app): hold `⌥ Space` on macOS or `Ctrl+Shift+Space` on Windows and Linux in any app, speak, and Izwi types what you said at the cursor. - **Transcription:** files or live audio, with speaker diarization, speaker-attributed transcripts, word timestamps, summaries, and translation on models that support it. - **Text to Speech and Studio:** built-in voices, voice cloning from a short sample, voice design from a description, and long-form projects edited segment by segment. - **Chat, Voices, and Models:** local chat, saved voices, and model download, load, and unload, with each model's real memory need shown before you download it. ### For developers The server speaks OpenAI's APIs at `http://localhost:8080/v1`, so the stock OpenAI SDKs work once you change the base URL. - Chat Completions with tool calling (forced and strict tool calls), and a preview of the Responses API. - Speech (WAV, MP3, Opus, FLAC, or PCM, whole or streamed), transcriptions, translations, and cloned voices (`/v1/audio/voices`). - Realtime (`/v1/realtime`): speech-to-speech sessions with unmodified OpenAI Realtime clients, including LiveKit Agents and Pipecat, with function and MCP tools. - Phone calls: live tr

# Agentic Attack Detections

[![validate](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/actions/workflows/validate.yml)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections)](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/releases)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections)](LICENSE)

Open-source detection rules, hunting queries and indicators for security teams. They cover agentic attack frameworks: tools that hand an intrusion to AI agents, which plan, run real attack tools and keep going until they reach a goal.

Free to use under the MIT license. Fixes, false-positive reports and new indicators are welcome.

## What is here

- **Framework folders.** ARTEX and its AntiFox fork, Cairn, PentAGI, HexStrike, CyberStrikeAI, Strix, Hermes Agent and Agent Zero. Each folder is built from a review of the framework's source code and the public reporting on its use.
- **Shared behaviors.** Rules for what these frameworks have in common, whatever the tool or the model behind it.
- **Indicators and feeds.** One CSV of 516 sourced indicators, and the feeds generated from it.

Formats: KQL for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR, Sigma, Suricata, Zeek, YARA and STIX 2.1, plus WAF rules for Cloudflare, AWS WAF and Azure WAF. Splunk and Elastic are covered by a Splunk app and Elastic rules for ARTEX, and by Sigma conversions for everything else.

## Try it in a minute

With Suricata installed, run the ARTEX rules over the sample capture in this repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections
cd agentic-attack-detections
mkdir -p out
suricata -r frameworks/artex/tests/artex-sample.pcap -S frameworks/artex/suricata/artex.rules -l out -k none
cat out/fast.log
```

You should see alerts such as:

```text
[1:3800001:1] TD ARTEX user agent artex-<role>/1.0
[1:3800020:1] TD ARTEX placeholder probe path
[1:3800023:2] TD Unsigned alg none JWT in URI
```

The capture is test traffic written from the framework source code and published reports. It is not a recorded intrusion.

CapCut Seedance: AI Video Generation Tool for Windows

A Windows reference and setup guide for CapCut Seedance, text-to-video synthesis, image animation, and the first-run workflow.

The tool sits on the CapCut video pipeline, so what you generate can flow directly into a familiar editing timeline. When you use CapCut Seedance you get a prompt-driven workspace, image animation with motion controls, and a set of preset visual effects that cover common short-form styles. A typical session moves from writing a prompt or dropping in a reference image, through previewing and adjusting motion strength, to exporting a clip you can refine further. The workflow is designed to be iterative, so you can regenerate variations quickly instead of rebuilding a project from scratch. candidates.description: Distill a good Claude Code / Codex session into a skill an open-weight model can follow to reproduce the task
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# skill-distill

A frontier model did a task well. Can an open-weight model do the same task, given the right instructions?

`skill-distill` is a skill for Claude Code or Codex (the **teacher**). You call it at the end of a good
session and name a **student**: an agent harness plus a model, for example omp with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
The teacher then loops:

1. reads the session and writes a skill for the student;
2. starts the student in tmux, on a fresh copy of the starting state, with the original prompt and the skill;
3. compares what the student produced with what the reference produced;
4. finds the first place the student went wrong and fixes the skill there;
5. runs again, three trials per version, until the student matches the reference.

You make the final call: the teacher shows you the reference and the student's best results side by side,
and the skill counts as done only when you accept it.

The result is two things: the reusable **operator skill** in this repo, and a **produced skill** for one task,
one model and one harness.

## Install

```
git clone https://github.com/sybil-solutions/skill-distill
ln -s "$PWD/skill-distill/skills/skill-distill" ~/.claude/skills/skill-distill    # Claude Code
ln -s "$PWD/skill-distill/skills/skill-distill" ~/.agents/skills/skill-distill    # Codex
```

Requirements: `tmux`, `git`, Python 3.10+, and the student harness installed and pointed at its model.
For web results, `pip install playwright pillow && playwright install chromium`.

## Use

At the end of a session that went well:

> distill this session into a skill for omp with deepseek-v4.1-flash on my local server

The teacher follows [`skills/skill-distill/SKILL.md`](skills/skill-distill/SKILL.md). You can watch the
students work with `tmux attach -t distill-<task>`.

## What's in it

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `skills/skill-distill/SKILL.md` | the loop the teacher follows |
| `skills/skill-distill/scripts/distill.py` | run bookkeeping: `init`, `trial`, `status`, `wait`, `evidence`, `verdict`, `ledger`, `report`, `accept` |
| `skills/skill-distill/scripts/extract_session.py` | Claude Code / Codex / omp session log → readable reference (drops system and AGENTS.md text) |
| `skills/skill-distill/scripts/capture_web.py` | serve a web app, drive it in headless Chromium, save screenshots and errors |
| `skills/skill-distill/adapters/` | one script per student harness: omp, pi, Codex, Claude Code, opencode |
| `skills/skill-distill/templates/student-skill/`

A training engine for your local model, using your idle compute.

Install • How it works • Commands • Roadmap • Website

Use your local model as usual through opencode, pi or any OpenAI-compatible tool. While you work, Songe notices what happens after each of the model's actions: the tool result, the error, your next message. When your agent is quiet, it teaches the model to see those coming. A new version is used only if it passes its checks, and nothing ever leaves your machine. ## ✨ Highlights - **Learns from how you work.** Your corrections, stated preferences and the tools' errors become lessons for your own model. - **Two kinds of Dreams.** A Quick Dream adds your preferences to the model's instructions in minutes; a Deep Dream trains the model itself while you are away. - **Safe by default.** A new version is used only if it does better on your own conversations; one click goes back to any earlier version. - **Stays out of the way.** Runs only when your agent is quiet, memory is free and the battery is fine, and stops the moment you are back. - **Private.** No account, no telemetry, no cloud.
